title: Orient MLCCs for the expected board stress
summary: Consider the direction of board strain when placing ceramic capacitors. Assembly or separation stress can crack a mechanically vulnerable MLCC.
verification: Review orientation and position against the actual bending process.
limitations: A universal rotation rule cannot cover every stress direction or separation method.

citations.locator: FAQ 0027, mechanical stress and component mounting orientation

title: Keep MLCCs out of screw-induced flex regions
summary: Review capacitors near mounting screws and provide assembly support that limits board bending.
applies_to: PCBs fastened to chassis or shields.
verification: Check board deflection during the intended fastening sequence.
limitations: No fixed hole clearance or torque is established here.

citations.locator: PDF pages 7 and 16, Mounting Capacitors Near Screw Holes; Tightening Screws

title: Choose depanelization with component strain in mind
summary: Plan capacitor placement alongside the actual panel-separation method. Manual bending can impose damaging strain.
required_inputs: Panel break lines and separator tooling
verification: Review separation strain and inspect representative assemblies.
limitations: Orientation advice for hand separation may not apply to disc cutting.

citations.locator: PDF pages 7 and 14, Board Separation and Board Separation Apparatus

title: Budget alignment for simultaneously mated connectors
summary: Budget relative connector placement and board tolerances against the selected series mating allowance when several connectors engage together.
verification: Check the combined alignment budget and trial assembly.
limitations: Do not copy alignment-pin or hole adjustments to unrelated connector families.

title: Reserve space for connector unmating and rework
summary: Reserve access for rework and a controlled unmating method, especially for multiple connectors or high separation forces.
verification: Review tool access and demonstrate assembly and removal.
limitations: Spacing and standoff selection depend on the connector and manufacturing process.

citations.locator: Page 2, rework spacing and jackscrew standoffs

title: Review shield gaps across the relevant frequency range
summary: Treat shield openings, seams and PCB-ground connections as possible leakage paths. Their electrical size changes with frequency.
applies_to: Board-level shields and enclosure shielding reviews.
verification: Test shielding with the production openings and assembly.
limitations: No universal aperture size or stitching pitch; cited examples focus on high-frequency shielding.

citations.locator: Pages 1-2, Shielding at millimeter wave frequencies

title: Include thermal materials in shield resonance review
summary: Evaluate the populated shield cavity, including thermal materials. Added dielectric or magnetic material can shift resonances and reduce shielding effectiveness.
applies_to: High-frequency board-level shields containing components or thermal interfaces.
verification: Compare measured or simulated shielding with the intended assembly.
limitations: Adding a shield or absorber does not guarantee improvement.

title: Preserve module antenna clearance in the enclosure
summary: Apply the selected module antenna keepout to both baseboard placement and the surrounding housing. Verify wireless performance in the final enclosure.
applies_to: ESP32-H2 modules with onboard PCB antennas.
verification: Inspect the antenna volume and test range and throughput in the assembled product.
limitations: This is module integration guidance, not antenna synthesis or a clearance rule for every wireless module.

citations.locator: General Principles of PCB Layout for Modules (Positioning a Module on a Base Board)

title: Verify flex contact mapping in the assembled orientation
summary: Connector contact side and flex folding can mirror or rotate the apparent pin order. Establish the assembled mapping before routing.
applies_to: Touch-panel flex interconnects and their mating boards.
required_inputs: Connector drawings, contact side and assembled folding path
verification: Trace each numbered contact through the assembled mating connection.
limitations: This mapping check does not establish bend radius, flex fatigue or connector life.
